transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes (recorded)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Liu (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (CTO, Copperline), Markus Hein (Platform Eng), Priya Shah (ML Eng)

Summary:
Quick discovery for Copperline's planned exit from OpenAI and move to a mixed hosting strategy. Evaluate parity with current outputs (OpenAI/Anthropic), feasibility of self-hosted vLLM/TGI routes vs Redwood Hosted/Dedicated/Private, security requirements (SOC2, VPC/KMS), and a pilot plan.

Topics covered:
- Current stack and constraints (OpenAI usage patterns, token volumes, latency targets)
- Compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI, finetuned LlamaX format, KV cache handling)
- Hosting tradeoffs: Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
- Security/compliance: SOC2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, data residency
- Next steps: pilot scope, benchmarks, pricing

Action items (captured above)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intro — maya here, im the AE supporting infra and migrations. we also have Ethan from solutions.
[00:12] Lena (Copperline): Hi all, lena. short version — we've been running mostly on OpenAI for orchestration and generation, some experiments with Anthropic, and a couple of internal POCs on vLLM. we're trying to get options: cheapest path that keeps latency and quality.
[00:26] Ethan (Redwood): great, thanks. can you outline current volumes and SLA needs? like p95 latency targets and tokens per month?
[00:34] Markus (Copperline): yeah, so volume: roughly 150M tokens / month now. bursty traffic with nightly batch jobs. p95 latency we want under 350 ms for the interactive flows, batch can be looser. cost is a big driver; OpenAI spend is about $35k/mo.
[00:49] Priya (Copperline): also important: we have a finetuned LlamaX model (converted to a tarball with custom adapters) and a small set of prompt templates. we tried vLLM locally but hit memory fragmentation and kv cache mismatch.
[01:05] Maya (Redwood): ok that's helpful. typical pattern we see: large prefix reuse we can cache, batching to lower unit cost, and quantization recommendations. question — what's the primary blocker for you right now?
[01:16] Lena: mostly cost + vendor lock. we also worry about eval parity — outputs with OpenAI are slightly different and the product team is picky about hallucination rates. if we switch infra, we need a clear regression test.
[01:30] Ethan: totally. our approach is twofold: 1) run eval parity on your canonical prompt set across the candidate runtime variants (OpenAI baseline, Redwood Hosted, Dedicated with tuned quantization, and a self-hosted vLLM/TGI path) and 2) measure latency/cost under a replay of your traffic.
[01:49] Markus: couple tech Qs: your runtime supports continuous KV caching and prefix caching? we rely on long context reuse. also how do you handle kv cache compatibility with vLLM save files — those are kind of brittle across versions.
[02:03] Ethan: we have an optimized runtime with continuous batching and KV cache management, but fair warning, vendor tooling names get transcribed funny — so i'll spell out: our caches are compatible with standard attention cache semantics, but when customers bring custom vLLM checkpoint dumps there can be mismatches. part of the compatibility scan is verifying model artifact format and kernel path.
[02:23] Priya: and TGI? we've used Triton inference server and TGI in our early experiments. conversion to Redwood — what does that look like?
[02:31] Maya: TGI is a common path. Redwood can serve models compiled for TGI or vLLM as long as the model artifact matches expected ops; for some internal ops we may recommend small recompile steps or a quant profile. we also provide Recommended quantization presets for the workload.
[02:49] Lena: security: we need SOC2, SAML SSO, KMS-backed encryption, and ability to restrict logs — basically we can't have training data leak. how do you handle audit logs and retention?
[03:01] Ethan: Redwood has SOC2 and audit log features on enterprise tiers; for Private deployment we can do customer-controlled KMS and keep logs in your VPC. Hosted plans include redacted logs by default; Dedicated offers more control and optional VPC peering.
[03:18] Markus: what's the lift to a Private on-prem box? we are not planning fully air gap but want VPC with our cloud provider and an on-prem option later.
[03:27] Maya: Private is heavier: control plane remains customer-managed for the VPC option, and fully on-prem includes an installable package. Usually we start with Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity) to get deterministic latency and then optionally move to Private if regulatory needs require.
[03:43] Priya: about eval parity — who runs the evals? do you do the golden baseline comparisons or do we need to run locally?
[03:51] Ethan: we can run the initial evals if you provide prompt set and sample model artifacts, or we can give you a runbook and tooling to reproduce. customers like a hybrid: we run a Redwood-hosted baseline for quick wins and then share scripts so Copperline can reproduce on their infra.
[04:06] Lena: sounds good. timeline — we want a pilot in the next 3 weeks, ideally a short pilot comparing Hosted vs Dedicated cost/latency and a self-hosted compatibility check. realistic?
[04:16] Maya: yes i think so. typical pilot: 1) quick artifact compatibility scan (2-3 days), 2) 48-hour perf runs with replayed traffic (we aim for week-long for stable metrics but 48 hours is a quick check), 3) cost projection and recommended config.
[04:31] Markus: do you support our model format — the finetuned LlamaX with adapters? we've got custom adapters that are not fully fused.
[04:38] Ethan: usually fine but adapter format matters; sometimes adapter weights need to be merged or we serve with a loader that applies adapters. that can add complexity for vLLM/TGI paths. we'll flag any conversion steps in the compatibility scan.
[04:51] Priya: ok one more — routing. if we go hybrid, can you route live traffic to Hosted and fall back to Dedicated or Private on overload? we want graceful degradation.
[04:59] Maya: yes, Smart routing is built-in — route by policy (latency/cost/region/customer tier) with fallback to compatible model variants. we can configure canary rollouts and A/B tests.
[05:11] Lena: great. any blockers on data retention and PII? we process user transcripts with potential PII, so we need redaction and a way to opt out of storing raw inputs.
[05:21] Ethan: Hosted environment supports request-level redaction and we can disable retention for tokens; Dedicated/Private gives you full control. we'll include retention policies in the security deck.
[05:33] Maya: ok i'll share SOC2 docs and the security slide deck after the call. also dedicated pricing and pilot template.
[05:40] Markus: about benchmarks — for latency, p95 350ms — do you have numbers for similar customers?
[05:47] Ethan: yes, with Dedicated + optimized quant profile we've seen p95 under 300ms for 2k token contexts on A100-equivalent. Hosted is often similar but depends on queueing and workload patterns. we'll pull anonymized benchmarks.
[05:59] Priya: cost — what's typical for our volume (150M tokens)? we want ballpark for Hosted vs Dedicated.
[06:05] Maya: rough ballpark: Hosted at current OpenAI parity might be similar or slightly cheaper depending on model size and quant; Dedicated has capitalized discounts if you commit to reserved capacity — we'll give concrete numbers in the pricing sheet.
[06:16] Lena: ok moving into details — integration effort: what SDKs and how long to swap our current OpenAI calls?
[06:23] Ethan: Redwood API is drop-in for generation/embeddings with small differences for streaming and function calls. many customers swap in a compatibility shim and point traffic to Redwood endpoints — often days to a week for initial integration, then the eval and tuning cycle.
[06:38] Markus: latency testing — can Redwood replay our traffic? we have a stored 72-hour sample trace.
[06:44] Maya: yes, we can replay traces for a throughput/latency run — depends on log format but usually straightforward. we'll take that as part of the pilot scope.
[06:53] Priya: about vLLM memory fragmentation — did you say you had kernel level patches?
[06:59] Ethan: our runtime selects kernels and optimizations and we have mitigations for fragmentation and streaming, but self-hosted vLLM is more operationally heavy; that's why Dedicated is often a middle ground.
[07:12] Lena: team/stakeholders — I'll loop in security and infra for the next call. we want a short exec summary for procurement too.
[07:20] Maya: noted. we'll prepare an exec one-pager and include clear success criteria: parity within X% metric on hallucination/F1, p95 latency under 350ms, and cost target under $X/month — we can fill numbers after we see your prompt set.
[07:38] Markus: any legal procurement caveats? data residency?
[07:42] Maya: for enterprise agreements we include data residency options and can scope SOW for Private deployment. legal typically reviews SLA and indemnities; we'll route to our legal ops.
[07:52] Priya: random question — do you support model version pinning and rollout policy?
[07:56] Ethan: yes versioning and rollouts, canary deploys and automated fallback on regressions.
[08:03] Lena: ok let's recap and close: we want compatibility scan, share prompts and artifacts, pilot perf run, security docs, and pricing.
[08:12] Maya: correct — i'll send the security pack + pricing + pilot template by monday (2026-04-12). Ethan will start the artifact compatibility work once you upload the tarball.
[08:22] Markus: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[08:25] Maya: thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
